rawFindings.title: Removing IP address handling breaks req.subdomains for IP hosts
rawFindings.explanation: Previously, the `req.subdomains` getter used the `isIP` function to detect if the host was an IP address. If so, it returned an array with the host as a single element, otherwise it split the host by '.' and reversed it. This change unconditionally splits the host by '.' and reverses it, removing special handling for IP addresses. This breaks behavior for IP hosts, causing them to be split incorrectly into octets or segments instead of treated as a single subdomain entry.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore IP address detection using `isIP` and return `[host]` as a single element array for IP addresses, e.g.: `var subdomains = !isIP(host) ? host.split('.').reverse() : [host];`

rawFindings.title: Removed IP address host handling in req.subdomains accessor
rawFindings.explanation: The original code used the net.isIP function to detect if the host is an IP address and returned an array with the host as a single element in that case, avoiding splitting the IP by dots. rawFindings.title: Regression in req.subdomains for IP address hosts
rawFindings.explanation: The patch changes the subdomains getter logic by removing the check for IP addresses using isIP(). Previously, when the host was an IP address (IPv4 or IPv6), the returned subdomains was an array containing the whole host string. After the change, the host is always split on '.', which breaks for IP addresses, causing incorrect splitting and invalid subdomain arrays.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the previous behavior that checks if the host is an IP address using isIP(), and if so, return an array containing the host string, otherwise split and reverse the host on '.'.
